eb3.name: EB-3

j1.name: J-1 Visa

j1.desc: For researchers, academics, trainees and specialists participating in approved exchange programs. Important two-year home residency rule may apply — understand it before applying.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions about U.S. visas and how Passly AI works.
faq.q1A: No. Passly AI provides educational information to help you understand possible immigration pathways. It does not constitute legal advice. Always consult a licensed immigration attorney before making any immigration decisions.
faq.q2A: Our scoring is based on official USCIS criteria and publicly available eligibility guidelines. Results are estimates, not guarantees. Individual cases vary significantly, and only a qualified attorney can evaluate your full situation.
faq.q3Q: Do I need to create an account?
faq.q3A: No account is required to complete the eligibility check. You can save your results by entering your email at the end.
faq.q4Q: How long does the questionnaire take?

faq.q6A: Yes! After completing the quiz, you can share your results as a card or save them for reference.

results.crossPathwayNotice: Your profile may qualify for both EB-1A and EB-2 NIW. These pathways share similar evidence requirements but apply different legal standards. Many applicants file both petitions simultaneously to establish the earliest possible priority date. An immigration attorney can help you decide the best strategy.

niw.weakestProng1Notice: The strongest NIW cases clearly define a specific proposed endeavor and connect it to documented national priorities. Generic descriptions of your profession are a common denial reason in 2025-2026.
niw.weakestProng2Notice: Building a documented record of success — through publications, measurable outcomes, or recognition from U.S. entities — significantly strengthens this prong.
niw.weakestProng3Notice: This is the most commonly challenged prong. It requires showing not just that your work is valuable, but specifically why the U.S. benefits more from waiving the job offer requirement than from requiring the standard labor certification process.
niw.highRfeNotice: Your profile shows potential for this pathway, but one or more areas may need strengthening before filing. An immigration attorney can help identify the gaps.
niw.context2026: 2025-2026 context: NIW denial rates exceeded approvals in Q4 2025. Non-STEM, non-healthcare endeavors with limited national impact documentation face the highest denial risk.

o1a.belowGate: Your profile doesn't yet meet the minimum threshold for O-1A (3 of 8 criteria), but you're building in the right direction. Focusing on these areas could make this pathway viable.
o1a.highRfe: Your profile meets the minimum criteria threshold, but evidence quality in one or more areas may trigger an RFE. An O-1A specialist attorney can help identify and strengthen weak points before filing.
o1a.c5Weak: The original contributions criterion (Criterion 5) is most frequently challenged in O-1A RFEs. Unaffiliated expert letters with specific impact statements — not generic praise — are essential.
o1a.context2025: FY2025: O-1 approval rate ~94%, RFE rate ~18.7%. Strongest stable visa category in 2025-2026. No annual cap, no lottery.

criteria.c1: National or international awards for excellence
criteria.c3: Published material ABOUT you and your work (not by you)
criteria.c4: Documented judging of others' work (peer review, competition judging)
criteria.c5: Original contributions of major significance (with unaffiliated expert letters)
criteria.c6: Scholarly articles in recognized field publications
criteria.c8: Critical or leading role in a distinguished-reputation organization
criteria.c9: High remuneration relative to field peers (with comparative data)

evidence.c5: Unaffiliated expert letters with SPECIFIC impact statements + citation data + third-party adoption evidence + real-world usage metrics
evidence.c4: Invitation letters from editors or organizers + confirmation of completed review + examples of work reviewed (anonymized)
evidence.c1: Award certificates + granting organization info + selection criteria documentation + media coverage of the award
evidence.c9: Offer letters/pay stubs + BLS comparison data + industry salary survey by role and location
evidence.c8: Org chart + letters from organizational leadership + evidence of org's distinguished reputation (revenue, rankings, media, awards, notable clients)

prong1: Specific description of proposed U.S. endeavor (not your job title or general field)
Industry reports or government data showing national demand in your field
BLS, NIH, DOE, or other agency data linking your field to national priorities
Evidence of interest from U.S. institutions or companies in your work (letters, agreements, invitations)
Publications or news coverage about the national importance of your specific endeavor field
prong2: Advanced degree diplomas and official transcripts (Master's, PhD, or equivalent)
Employment letters showing progressive responsibility and leadership roles in the field
Publications, patents, or other documented project outcomes with measurable impact
Letters from U.S. experts specifically describing your expertise and its impact
Quantifiable metrics: citations, users, revenue generated, adoption rates, project reach
prong3: Evidence of self-employment, contracts with multiple clients, or that the PERM process is impractical for your situation
Letters from U.S. entities expressing specific need for your expertise (not simply character references)
Documentation that your contributions benefit the U.S. regardless of competing U.S. worker availability
Concrete business plan or U.S. activities plan with specific milestones
Evidence of urgency or uniqueness: documented field shortage, time-critical impact, third-party adoption

o1.name: O-1 Visa
o1.fullName: O-1 Visa: Individuals with Extraordinary Ability
o1.tagline: For people at the top of their field
o1.description: The O-1 visa is for individuals who have demonstrated extraordinary ability in sciences, arts, education, business, or athletics. It requires showing sustained national or international acclaim through awards, publications, speaking engagements, critical roles, or high compensation.

h1b.name: H-1B Visa
h1b.tagline: The most common work visa for professionals
h1b.description: The H-1B allows U.S. companies to employ foreign workers in specialty occupations requiring theoretical or technical expertise. A bachelor's degree or higher (or equivalent) in a related field is typically required. Subject to an annual lottery cap.

eb2niw.name: EB-2 NIW
eb2niw.tagline: A green card without an employer sponsor
eb2niw.description: The EB-2 NIW allows individuals with advanced degrees or exceptional ability to self-petition for a green card if their work is in the national interest of the United States. No employer sponsor is required.

f1.name: F-1 Visa
f1.description: The F-1 visa allows international students to pursue academic studies at accredited U.S. universities and language programs. Students must maintain full-time enrollment and demonstrate nonimmigrant intent.

l1.name: L-1 Visa
l1.description: The L-1 allows multinational companies to transfer employees in managerial, executive, or specialized knowledge roles to a U.S. office. The L-1A is for managers and executives; the L-1B for specialized knowledge workers.

e2.name: E-2 Visa
e2.description: The E-2 treaty investor visa allows nationals of treaty countries to invest a substantial amount in a U.S. business and direct its operations. The business must not be marginal and the investor must have controlling interest.

b1b2.name: B-1/B-2 Visa
b1b2.description: The B-1/B-2 visa allows temporary visits to the U.S. for business (B-1) or tourism and personal reasons (B-2). Applicants must demonstrate strong ties to their home country and nonimmigrant intent.

eb1a.name: EB-1A Green Card
eb1a.tagline: A self-petitioned green card — no employer sponsor required
eb1a.description: The EB-1A provides a direct path to a green card for individuals who have risen to the very top of their field — in sciences, arts, business, education, or athletics. No employer sponsor or job offer is required. Based on the same legal standard as the O-1A visa.

eb2perm.name: EB-2 PERM
eb2perm.fullName: EB-2 PERM: Employer-Sponsored Advanced Degree Green Card
eb2perm.tagline: A green card through employer sponsorship and labor certification
eb2perm.description: The EB-2 PERM is a green card sponsored by a U.S. employer for professionals with advanced degrees or exceptional ability. Requires a permanent job offer, a labor certification process through the Department of Labor (PERM), and an I-140 immigrant petition.
